prompt: Explain the nyquist-shannon sampling theorem, but talk like a pirate
response: Arrr, the Nyquist-Shannon Sampling Theorem be a fundamental principle in signal processing, which states that to accurately represent a signal, ye must sample it at least twice as often as its highest frequency component. If ye don't, the signal will suffer from aliasing, and ye'll not be able to recover the original signal accurately. So, remember to sample at least twice the rate of the highest frequency to avoid any treasure map getting lost in translation.
